No, that is not true. In Switzerland, the retirement age for women is currently set at 64 years old, but this is part of a gradual reform process. The retirement age for women is being raised to align with that of men (65 years). The exact timeline for this change depends on the year of birth:

- Women born in 1960 or later will retire at 64.
- Women born before 1960 will retire at 63 or 64, depending on their specific birth year.

Additionally, early retirement is possible under certain conditions, and the retirement age can be adjusted based on individual circumstances and pension regulations.
